slot.brief: Diagram of a system of charges or a non-uniform charge distribution (e.g., charged sphere, shell, or cavity); ask for field at a point using Gauss's law with symmetry arguments.

stem: An infinitely long non-conducting cylinder of radius $R$ has a uniform volume charge density $\rho$. A cylindrical cavity of radius $R/3$ is made with its axis parallel to the axis of the cylinder and at a distance $R/2$ from it, as shown in the figure. The point $P$ lies on the boundary of the cavity such that the line joining the cavity axis to $P$ is perpendicular to the line joining the axis of the cylinder to the cavity axis. The magnitude and direction of the electric field at $P$ is:
options: $\dfrac{\rho R}{4\varepsilon_0}$, directed perpendicular to the line joining the axes
$\dfrac{\rho R}{4\varepsilon_0}$, directed from the cylinder axis towards the cavity axis
$\dfrac{\rho R}{6\varepsilon_0}$, directed from the cylinder axis towards the cavity axis
$\dfrac{\rho R}{3\varepsilon_0}$, directed from the cylinder axis towards the cavity axis
working: By superposition, \(\vec{E}_{\text{net}} = \vec{E}_{\text{full cylinder}} - \vec{E}_{\text{removed cylinder}}\). Inside a uniformly charged infinite cylinder, \(\vec{E} = \frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}\), where \(\vec{r}\) is the radial vector from its axis. Let the cavity axis be at displacement \(\vec{d}\) from the cylinder axis (magnitude \(d = R/2\)). For a point \(P\) inside the cavity with position vector \(\vec{r}_{P}\) relative to the cavity axis, \(\vec{E}_{\text{full}} = \frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}(\vec{d}+\vec{r}_{P})\) and \(\vec{E}_{\text{removed}} = \frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}_{P}\). Hence \(\vec{E}_{\text{net}} = \frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec{d}\). The magnitude is \(\frac{\rho d}{2\varepsilon_0} = \frac{\rho (R/2)}{2\varepsilon_0} = \frac{\rho R}{4\varepsilon_0}\), directed from the cylinder axis to the cavity axis.
solution:
By superposition, treat the cavity as a cylinder of charge density $-\rho$. For a uniformly charged infinite cylinder, $\vec E=\dfrac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec r$, so at $P$ the field is
$$\vec E_{\text{net}}=\frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}(\vec d+\vec r_P)-\frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec r_P=\frac{\rho}{2\varepsilon_0}\vec d.$$
With $d=R/2$, the magnitude is $\dfrac{\rho R}{4\varepsilon_0}$, directed from the cylinder axis towards the cavity axis.

figure.description: Cross‑sectional view of an infinitely long cylinder. The outer circle has radius R and centre O. A smaller circle of radius R/3 is drawn inside, with centre C at a horizontal distance R/2 from O; the small circle represents the cylindrical cavity. Point P is marked on the circumference of the small circle such that line CP is perpendicular to line OC (e.g., CP is drawn vertically upward from C). Labels O, C, P are shown. The distance OC is labelled R/2 and the radius CP is labelled R/3.
